narrative:
A.S. Watson Group (int-watsons) engagement ran all three passes — secrets, buckets, takeovers — across 122 scope assets spanning 10 brands (Watsons, Park N Shop, Fortress, LookAtMe, Drogas, Moneyback) in 9+ countries. The result was a clean triple-negative: 0 verified secrets, 0 listable buckets, 0 confirmed takeover candidates. The engagement's primary value was validating the new subzy_body_recheck_required gate (added 30 minutes before the run based on bc-seek learnings) and uncovering two new FP-class patterns that expand the known false-positive taxonomy.

The secrets pass exposed a structural problem with the brand name 'watsons' as a code-search base name: IBM Watson AI (ibm-mas, watson-developer-cloud, ibm-client-engineering, WatsonX SDK) generates 25–30 false-positive hits per dork, making bare-stem code search meaningless for this program. The Pass B domain-qualified queries (watsons.com.hk/env, drogas.lt/env, etc.) all returned 0 hits, confirming there is no GitHub footprint for A.S. Watson Group's operational infrastructure. The as-watson org exists but has 0 public repos; 14 other org-name candidates all 404'd. This is a structurally different problem from operator negligence — A.S. Watson is a conglomerate operating in Asia and Europe where public GitHub presence is not part of their engineering culture. Future secret-hunting on this program should skip Pass A entirely and skip bare 'watsons' in Pass B dorks; domain-qualified queries are the only viable approach.

The buckets pass confirmed the 9th consecutive engagement with 100% s3scanner ACL false-positive rate: 13 flagged candidates, 13 AccessDenied on recheck. No ownership verification was needed. The bare 'watsons' bucket (ap-south-1) is the brand stem and warrants a basename_skip entry for the same structural reasons as prior bare-stem entries (indrive, snapchat, seek, etc.) — IBM Watson SDK overlap makes GH code-search Check A degenerate for this name specifically.

The takeovers pass provided the first end-to-end validation of rule-takeover_hunter-subzy_body_recheck_required-e91f7. Subzy flagged 3 candidates VULNERABLE; all 3 failed body recheck and were disqualified. Two new FP classes emerged: (1) Cargo Collective fingerprint on an AWS ELB CNAME — the same FP class as the bc-seek SendGrid finding, confirming the pattern generalises to any generic 404-serving infrastructure, not just SendGrid edge. (2) Emarsys (SAP) / Unbounce fingerprint collision — two independent instances in one engagement (suite16.emarsys.net for Turkey, suite40.emarsys.net for Hong Kong), providing strong dual corroboration. The emarsys.net cname_hub_skip rule was auto-written mid-run by the takeover-hunter agent (rule-takeover_hunter-cname_hub_skip-a3f91, confidence medium, already in rules.json). This is the first confirmed instance of mid-run rule auto-codification by a subagent — the entry appears correct on inspection, but the ID was computed from a different canonical form than retro-analyzer would produce (a3f91 vs the b9b9d this retro computes), indicating the agent used non-canonical field ordering. This is a process hygiene concern worth monitoring: auto-added rules should still pass through retro review for consistency, and agents should be reminded the canonical form requires sort_keys=True in JSON serialization.

Recommended pre-flight for next int-watsons run: skip Pass A (0 public repos, no footprint); skip bare 'watsons' in Pass B dorks (IBM Watson collision, use watsons.com.hk/watsons.co.th etc. only); skip Emarsys CNAMEs in takeover pass (cname_hub_skip already applied); note that Akamai EdgeKey (*.aswatson.com.edgekey.net) and AWS ELB are the dominant infrastructure patterns — neither is a subdomain-takeover target.
